walk.title: Solve it: Harvest Lane's first three automations
walk.sample: One week of Tolu's admin diary · 270 orders a week · 9 admin steps

steps.say: Tolu spends almost four hours a day moving information around. Before we touch any tool, we find out which parts a machine should take.
show: 45 orders a day · 6 days a week

steps.say: We start with a week of real data. Tolu writes down every admin step, how often it happens and how long it takes, because a measured week beats a guess.
show: Step · runs per week · minutes per run

steps.say: Now we score each row. Runs times minutes gives the time; the error factor makes costly mistakes count more.
Then we divide by difficulty, never multiply, so hard tasks drop down the list. Keep every row in per-week units.
Sort by priority. Copying orders into the notebook leads at 540, then the total and the payment check at 270 each.
Notice reading the WhatsApp order scores lowest, at 45. Keep an eye on it, because the next step pulls it back in.
The ranking says automate copying first, but copying needs the order in a clean shape, and reading messy WhatsApp text is hard. So we check what depends on what.
Here's the key move: change the input, not just the steps. A short order form makes the order arrive already structured, and steps one to four collapse into one automation.
show: Input: order form or WhatsApp menu

steps.say: We choose three. Order capture first, then payment confirmation from a payment link, then a stock update that rides on the clean order data.
Route planning stays with a person on purpose. It happens six times a week and needs local judgment.
show: Later quick wins: thank-you, weekly summary

steps.say: Last, the payback. Eighteen hours saved a week, worth about one hundred and ninety-three thousand naira a month if Tolu's hour is worth two thousand five hundred.
show: Saved: 1,080 of 1,358 min a week ≈ 18 h

walk.end: Measured pain, scored honestly, dependencies checked: that's how you pick what to automate. Now score five tasks of your own.

walk.title: Solve it: will it rain on tomorrow's deliveries?
walk.sample: Ibadan forecast from Open-Meteo · a fake payment.success webhook for order HL-0042

steps.say: Two jobs today, both by hand: ask a weather service about tomorrow's rain, then watch a payment notice arrive. No platform yet, so you see what the platforms hide.
Open-Meteo is free and needs no key for non-commercial use. Its docs builder writes the URL for us, so we never guess parameter names.
In Hoppscotch, set the method to GET and paste the forecast address. Hoppscotch splits it into the same parameter table you'll fill on an HTTP step later.
The time zone matters. Without it, tomorrow could mean tomorrow in London, and late at night you'd read the wrong day.
Press Send. We want status two hundred, OK, and a JSON body.
Read the shape. The daily lists line up by position: position zero is today, position one is tomorrow.
Now a simple rule: fifty per cent or more, the riders pack covers. Seventy is above fifty, so tonight's message is pack covers. No AI needed; it's a number against a threshold.
Break it on purpose. Remove latitude and you get a four hundred, Bad Request. Misspell forecast and you get a four oh four, wrong address.
Now flip roles. Webhook.site gives you a unique URL that plays Harvest Lane's system, and records anything sent to it.
Send a pretend payment notice for order HL-0042 and watch it appear instantly. That's a webhook: the doorbell, not the mailbox.
steps.data: request received with headers and body

steps.say: One trap: the amount is in kobo, not naira. One million two hundred and fifty thousand kobo is twelve thousand five hundred naira, so check the unit before any maths.

walk.end: You've been the client and the server. Every HTTP step and webhook trigger in this course is just this, wrapped in a nicer screen.

walk.title: Solve it: turn a WhatsApp order into clean cargo
walk.sample: Mrs Adebayo · 2 crates of tomatoes + 1 big bag of tatashe · Tuesday afternoon · 14 Ring Road

steps.say: A real order arrived on WhatsApp on Monday morning. We'll turn it into JSON any automation could use, then work out the total from paths.
Read it the way a machine would need it: who, what, and where and when. And Tuesday after Monday the fifth is the sixth of October.
show: Where/when: address, day, time of day

steps.say: Choose a type for every field before writing anything. The phone is a string, because you never add phone numbers, and that keeps the country code safe.
Products go in an array, because an order can have any number of them. Paid is a true or false, and notes is null on purpose.
Now write it. Customer and delivery become objects, and each product gets a stable sku, so later steps don't care how someone spells tatashe.
Money stays a plain number with no naira sign or commas, and the date is ISO, so nothing can be misread.
Test it in the lab. Tap a path and see the value and its type. Remember, counting starts at zero.
Try items two. There are only two items, so it comes back empty. That's the most common beginner bug.
Calculate the total from paths: each quantity times its price, plus the delivery fee.
Only when we show it to Mrs Adebayo does it become thirty-five thousand five hundred naira with a sign. Inside the data it stays a number.
Spreadsheets can't hold a list in one cell, so we flatten it: one row in Orders, one row per item in Order items, linked by the order ID.

walk.end: Right types, clear paths, a total you can trust. In Module 0.5 you'll make AI produce exactly this JSON from any messy message.

walk.title: Solve it: rebuild Harvest Lane's order sheet
walk.sample: Tolu's Orders_final_2 tab · order HL-0043 for Mrs Adebayo · two Mrs Ades

steps.say: This is Tolu's real order tab. It was built for Tolu's eyes, so it breaks every automation. We'll rebuild it so machines, and Tolu, can trust it.
show: Two customers both called Mrs Ade

steps.say: Go rule by rule. There's a title above the headers, several products crammed into one cell, and an amount column mixing text and numbers.
show: Rule 2: "2 tomato, 1 tatashe" in one cell

steps.say: There's a total row and a blank row inside the data, VIP shown only by colour, and no IDs, so the two Mrs Ades are the same person to a machine.
steps.data: phones lost zeros · 4 spellings of paid

steps.say: Everything with its own identity gets its own tab: customers, products, orders, and the items inside each order.
Each tab has an ID in column A, and the many side stores the ID of the one side. Orders point to a customer; items point to an order and a product.
Now formulas, in row two, filled down. The customer's name is looked up by ID, with a clear message if it's not found.
The order total is calculated, never typed: add up the line totals that belong to this order, then the delivery fee.
Notice the unit price is stored on each item, not looked up. Prices change, and last month's orders must still show what the customer actually paid.
Load order HL-0043: one Orders row and two item rows. The total should match our hand calculation from Module 0.3.
Now the Mrs Ade test. Look up order HL-0045 by name and you might get the wrong lady. Look it up by customer ID and it's always the one in Mokola.
steps.data: by ID: right address every time

steps.say: Finally, lock the inputs. Status becomes a dropdown that rejects anything else, because a machine sees Paid and paid as different words.
Phones become plain text so the zero survives, yes or no fields become checkboxes, and the formula columns are protected so nobody types over them.

walk.end: One table per job, IDs for every link, totals that calculate themselves: that's a sheet every automation in this course can read and write.

walk.title: Solve it: a prompt that turns any order into clean JSON
walk.sample: 10 test messages in English, Pidgin and Yoruba · e.g. "abeg bring 3 bag onion come Bodija tomorrow morning"

steps.say: Customers still type orders in English, Pidgin and Yoruba. We'll write a prompt that turns them into clean JSON, and prove it with a test, not a hope.
show: Goal: 10 out of 10 on the test set

steps.say: Build the exam before the student. Ten messages, normal and tricky, each with the right answer written down first.
show: #10 a price question, not an order

steps.say: Version one is the obvious one-line prompt. It looks fine on message one, but on the full set only four answers are usable.
show: Extract the order from this customer message as JSON.

steps.say: Look at why. Markdown fences break the parser, an address and quantity were invented, and ugwu became pepper.
Version two adds a role, the SKU catalogue, only JSON, null when something isn't stated, and ISO dates from today's date.
Two still fail, because customers say rodo and the red one, and the catalogue only knew scotch bonnet.
show: Message 9: guessed rodo for "the red one"

steps.say: Version three teaches the model our world: the local names customers really use, and one worked example in Pidgin.
show: PEP-ROF-L rodo / ata rodo / scotch bonnet

steps.say: It also gets a needs confirmation flag. Anything uncertain, or not an order at all, is marked for a human to check.
Compare the three versions side by side. Each one fixed the failures the last one revealed, and you can see it in the score.
Check the hard ones. Message ten is a price question, so items is empty and it's flagged for Tolu.
Notice what the AI is not allowed to do: no prices and no totals. The sheet from Module 0.4 does the maths with formulas.
And a rules step checks every answer: does it parse, are the SKUs real, is every quantity above zero? Anything that fails goes to Tolu, not the sheet.

walk.end: Tested on ten messages, scored, and improved until it passed: that's a prompt you can put inside an automation.

walk.title: Solve it: the leaked key, and closing every open door
walk.sample: Leaked AI key sk-live-8f2a… · a former rider who can still edit Orders · Harvest Lane's tools

steps.say: Tolu's AI key is public and being used. In the first ten minutes, Nodo revokes it and pastes a new one into the single credential the automations use. Revoke first, investigate after.
show: Deleting the screenshot is not enough

steps.say: Then we find every other open door with an access register: one sheet listing every tool, who or what has access, at what level, and where its secret lives.
We build it with the rules from Module 0.4: one header row, one row per access. That makes it easy to filter by person when someone leaves.
show: One row = one person or app on one tool

steps.say: Every tool runs through one business account, not Tolu's personal one. Tolu owns the Orders sheet, with two-factor on.
The former rider is gone. Riders now only see a separate today's deliveries file, as viewers, with no customer data in it. That's least privilege.
The new AI key lives only in the Zapier connection, with a ten dollar monthly cap, so the next leak is a small problem instead of a four hundred dollar one.
Paystack is still being built, so Make holds the test secret key in its keychain. Only Tolu switches anything to live.
Now the one-page policy, short enough that staff actually read it. First, keys and passwords: keys live only in the platform or the password manager, never in chats, sheets or AI tools.
show: 1. Keys only in platform or password manager
2. Never in chats, sheets, docs, AI, screenshots

steps.say: Every provider gets a spending cap and an alert, and two-factor is on for email, automation tools, AI providers and banking.
show: 4. Monthly cap and alert on every provider

steps.say: Access goes to named people at the lowest level, and leavers lose it the same day. Customer data is collected only for orders, and only needed fields go to AI.
show: 6–8. Named people, same-day removal, quarterly review

steps.say: And the five words to remember if something leaks: revoke, replace, check usage, tell Tolu, fix the cause.

walk.end: One register, one page of rules: the next leak becomes a ten-minute fix instead of a four hundred dollar bill.

items.name: HL · Invoices → Drive
items.what: Every attachment that lands in the Gmail label Invoices is uploaded to the Google Drive folder Harvest Lane → Supplier invoices, named after who sent it and what it is. Two steps, so it fits the free plan.
steps: 1 · Trigger · Gmail › New Attachment: account = the Harvest Lane business Gmail; Label/Mailbox = Invoices; Search String = -in:sent. Test trigger with a real emailed PDF and pick that record as sample data.

2 · Action · Google Drive › Upload File: account = the same business Google account; Drive = My Google Drive; Folder = Harvest Lane → Supplier invoices; File = the attachment file pill from step 1 (the entry marked as a file, not the attachment's name or link); File name = [1. From Name] - [1. Subject] - [1. Attachment Name] (pills joined with the fixed text " - ").
setup: Use the Harvest Lane business Google account from Module 0.6, not a personal one.
In Gmail, create a label called Invoices.
In Gmail Settings → Filters and blocked addresses → Create a new filter: match your suppliers' addresses plus "has attachment", and apply the label Invoices.
In Google Drive, create the folder Harvest Lane → Supplier invoices.
In Zapier, create a new Zap and build the two steps exactly as listed. Connect Gmail and Google Drive with the business account, and read each permission screen before allowing.
Rename the Zap to HL · Invoices → Drive and click Publish.
To share it as a template: open the Zap's menu, choose Share, and copy the share link.
items.test: Email yourself a small PDF from another address so it lands in Invoices, then Test trigger and Test step: the PDF appears in Supplier invoices named like Farmgate Supplies - Invoice 0192 - inv_0192.pdf. After publishing, send a second invoice: within about 15 minutes (free plan polling) it appears in Drive with no clicks, and Zap history shows the run with the data in and out of each step.
items.tasks: One task per attachment saved (only the Drive upload counts; Gmail polling does not), so about 25 tasks a month for Tolu's 25 invoices.

walk.title: Build it: supplier invoices file themselves
walk.sample: Email from Farmgate Supplies · Invoice 0192 · inv_0192.pdf · label Invoices

steps.say: Our trigger is Gmail, New Attachment. Gmail's own filter already labels supplier invoices, so we only watch that one label.
We add a search string so attachments you send yourself, like quotes to customers, are never filed as supplier invoices.
Connect the business account, not your personal one, and read the permission screen before you click allow. Then test with a real emailed PDF.
show: Test trigger → pick the real email

steps.say: Now the action: Google Drive, Upload File, into the Supplier invoices folder.
For the File field, pick the pill that carries the actual file. A name or link pill only gives you a tiny text file.
show: File: attachment file pill from step 1

steps.say: The file name mixes pills with fixed text, so every invoice says who sent it and what it is.
Test the step, check Drive, name the Zap, then publish. Nothing runs by itself until you publish.

walk.end: That's the whole Zap. Build it yourself, publish it, then open Zap history after the next live invoice.

items.name: HL · Form order → Sheet + alert
items.what: One nine-step Zap: a Google Form order is cleaned (phone, date), priced from the Products sheet, given a delivery fee by area (with a fallback), totalled, saved as a clean row in Orders with the total as a plain number, and emailed to Tolu with the total shown in naira.
steps: 1 · Trigger · Google Forms › New Form Response: Form = the order form from 1.1 Bronze (name, phone, product, quantity, delivery date) with an Area dropdown added.

2 · Action · Formatter by Zapier › Numbers › Format Phone Number (rename step "Clean phone"): Input = [1. Phone]; Country code = Nigeria (NG); To Format = international format without spaces (E.164 or similar, e.g. +2348031234567).
3 · Action · Formatter by Zapier › Date/Time › Format (rename step "Clean date"): Input = [1. Delivery date]; To Format = YYYY-MM-DD; To Timezone = Africa/Lagos.

4 · Action · Google Sheets › Lookup Spreadsheet Row: Spreadsheet = your 0.4 workbook; Worksheet = Products; Lookup Column = name; Lookup Value = [1. Product]; tick the option to stop or flag the Zap if nothing is found. Returns the whole row (sku, price_ngn).
5 · Action · Formatter by Zapier › Utilities › Lookup Table: Lookup Key = [1. Area]; Lookup Table rows: Bodija = 1500, Mokola = 1500, Ring Road = 1500, Challenge = 2000; Fallback Value = 2500.
6 · Action · Formatter by Zapier › Numbers › Spreadsheet-Style Formula: Formula = [1. Quantity] * [4. price_ngn] + [5. Value] (e.g. 2 * 12500 + 1500 = 26500).
7 · Action · Formatter by Zapier › Numbers › Format Currency: Input = [6. Output]; Currency = NGN; Currency Locale = English (Nigeria) if listed. Output like ₦26,500.00, used only in the email.

8 · Action · Google Sheets › Create Spreadsheet Row: Spreadsheet = your 0.4 workbook; Worksheet = Orders; name = [1. Name]; phone = [2. Output]; delivery date = [3. Output]; sku = [4. sku]; unit price = [4. price_ngn]; quantity = [1. Quantity]; area = [1. Area]; delivery fee = [5. Value]; total = [6. Output] (the plain number); status = New.

9 · Action · Gmail › Send Email: To = Tolu's address (e.g. tolu@harvestlane.example); Subject = New order · [1. Name] · [3. Output] · [7. Output]; Body = each order field on its own line (name, phone from step 2, product, quantity, delivery date from step 3, area, fee from step 5, total from step 7).
setup: Multi-step Zaps need a paid Zapier plan or a trial of paid features.
Set your Zapier account time zone to Africa/Lagos (Settings) before building.
Add an Area dropdown (Bodija, Mokola, Ring Road, Challenge, …) to the order form from 1.1 Bronze.
Have the 0.4 workbook ready: a Products tab with headers name, sku, price_ngn in row 1, and an Orders tab with its header row in row 1.
Connect Google Forms, Google Sheets and Gmail with the Harvest Lane business Google account.
Build the nine steps in order, renaming each Formatter step (Clean phone, Clean date, Delivery fee, Total, Total for email) so the Zap reads like a recipe.
Test each step top to bottom, name the Zap HL · Form order → Sheet + alert, and Publish. Share it from the Zap's menu → Share to get the template link.
items.test: Submit a deliberately messy response: name "mrs ADEBAYO ", phone "0803 123 4567", product Tomatoes (crate), quantity 2, date 6 October, area Bodija. Orders gets a row with phone +2348031234567, date 2026-10-06, unit price 12500, fee 1500 and total 26500 (a number); Tolu's email subject ends with ₦26,500.00. A second order from an unlisted area (e.g. Apete) gets fee 2500.
items.tasks: About three tasks per order: the two Google Sheets steps and the Gmail step count, while the five Formatter steps use no tasks (check Zapier's pricing page for exact counting on searches).

walk.title: Build it: the one-Zap order line
walk.sample: mrs ADEBAYO · 0803 123 4567 · 2 tomato crates · 6 October · Bodija

steps.say: The order form is our trigger. Test it with deliberately messy data, so you can prove every cleaning step works.
First station: clean the phone number into one international format the riders' dialler understands.
Next we clean the date into the format we store, in Lagos time, so nothing is an hour off.
Prices change, so we look them up in the Products sheet Tolu controls. If the product isn't found, the Zap stops instead of pricing it at nothing.
Delivery fee comes from a small lookup table. The fallback charges a safe default for any new area, so the fee is never blank.
Now the maths: quantity times price, plus the fee.
We make a naira version of the total, but only for the email a person reads.
Save the clean row. Map the cleaned phone and date, and store the plain number total so the sheet can add it up.
Finally, tell Tolu with a readable summary. Test every step, name the Zap, and publish.
show: Subject: New order · name · date · total

walk.end: Nine steps, one Zap, about three tasks. Build it yourself, then check three totals by hand.

items.name: HL · Form order → routed (Filter + Paths)
items.what: The 1.2 order Zap with a junk filter and a junction: test orders stop before any task is used, orders over ₦50,000 go to Tolu at once as PRIORITY (with a Logistics row if out of zone), out-of-zone orders go to the Logistics tab, and everything else takes the standard route. Every order takes exactly one branch.
steps: 1 · Trigger · Google Forms › New Form Response: Form = the order form from 1.1 Bronze with the Area dropdown from 1.2 (name, phone, product, quantity, delivery date, area).
2 · Filter by Zapier (rename "Drop test orders"): Only continue if… [1. Name] (Text) Does not contain test. Test orders stop here and show as Filtered in Zap history.

3 · Formatter by Zapier › Numbers › Format Phone Number ("Clean phone"): Input = [1. Phone]; Country code = Nigeria (NG); To Format = international without spaces (E.164 or similar, e.g. +2348031234567).
4 · Formatter by Zapier › Date/Time › Format ("Clean date"): Input = [1. Delivery date]; To Format = YYYY-MM-DD; To Timezone = Africa/Lagos.

5 · Google Sheets › Lookup Spreadsheet Row ("Price from Products"): Spreadsheet = your 0.4 workbook; Worksheet = Products; Lookup Column = name; Lookup Value = [1. Product]; tick the option to stop or flag the Zap if nothing is found. Returns sku and price_ngn.
6 · Formatter by Zapier › Utilities › Lookup Table ("Delivery fee"): Lookup Key = [1. Area]; rows Bodija = 1500, Mokola = 1500, Ring Road = 1500, Challenge = 2000; Fallback Value = 2500.
7 · Formatter by Zapier › Utilities › Lookup Table ("Zone"): Lookup Key = [1. Area]; rows Bodija = inside, Mokola = inside, Ring Road = inside, Challenge = inside; Fallback Value = outside.
8 · Formatter by Zapier › Numbers › Spreadsheet-Style Formula ("Total"): Formula = [1. Quantity] * [5. price_ngn] + [6. Value].
9 · Formatter by Zapier › Numbers › Format Currency ("Total for email"): Input = [8. Output]; Currency = NGN; Currency Locale = English (Nigeria) if listed. Used only in emails.
10 · Paths by Zapier ("Route order"), three branches, checked left to right:
10A · Path A · Priority: Only continue if… [8. Output] (Number) Greater than 50000. (Always the plain number from step 8, never step 9's ₦ text.)

10A.1 · Google Sheets › Create Spreadsheet Row: Spreadsheet = your 0.4 workbook; Worksheet = Orders; name = [1. Name]; phone = [3. Output]; delivery date = [4. Output]; sku = [5. sku]; unit price = [5. price_ngn]; quantity = [1. Quantity]; area = [1. Area]; delivery fee = [6. Value]; total = [8. Output] (the plain number); status = New.

10A.2 · Gmail › Send Email: To = Tolu (e.g. tolu@harvestlane.example); Subject = PRIORITY · New order · [1. Name] · [4. Output] · [9. Output]; Body = each order field on its own line (name, phone from step 3, product, quantity, delivery date from step 4, area, zone from step 7, fee from step 6, total from step 9).
10A.3 · Filter by Zapier ("Out of zone?"): Only continue if… [7. Value] (Text) Exactly matches outside.

10A.4 · Google Sheets › Create Spreadsheet Row: Spreadsheet = your 0.4 workbook; Worksheet = Logistics; name = [1. Name]; phone = [3. Output]; delivery date = [4. Output]; area = [1. Area]; zone = [7. Value]; product = [1. Product]; quantity = [1. Quantity]; total = [8. Output].

10B · Path B · Outside zone: Only continue if… [8. Output] (Number) Less than 50001 AND [7. Value] (Text) Exactly matches outside. ("Less than 50001" = 50,000 or less, so a big out-of-zone order can't match both A and B.)

10B.1 · Google Sheets › Create Spreadsheet Row: Spreadsheet = your 0.4 workbook; Worksheet = Orders; name = [1. Name]; phone = [3. Output]; delivery date = [4. Output]; sku = [5. sku]; unit price = [5. price_ngn]; quantity = [1. Quantity]; area = [1. Area]; delivery fee = [6. Value]; total = [8. Output] (the plain number); status = New.

10B.2 · Google Sheets › Create Spreadsheet Row: Spreadsheet = your 0.4 workbook; Worksheet = Logistics; name = [1. Name]; phone = [3. Output]; delivery date = [4. Output]; area = [1. Area]; zone = [7. Value]; product = [1. Product]; quantity = [1. Quantity]; total = [8. Output].
10C · Path C · Standard: set as the fallback branch (rightmost; runs only when A and B didn't match).

10C.1 · Google Sheets › Create Spreadsheet Row: Spreadsheet = your 0.4 workbook; Worksheet = Orders; name = [1. Name]; phone = [3. Output]; delivery date = [4. Output]; sku = [5. sku]; unit price = [5. price_ngn]; quantity = [1. Quantity]; area = [1. Area]; delivery fee = [6. Value]; total = [8. Output] (the plain number); status = New.
10C.2 · Gmail › Send Email: To = Tolu; Subject = New order · [1. Name] · [4. Output] · [9. Output]; Body = each order field on its own line, as in 1.2.
setup: Filters are on every plan; Paths and multi-step Zaps need a paid plan or a trial of paid features. Set your Zapier account time zone to Africa/Lagos.
Start from your 1.2 Zap (duplicate it) or build fresh. Insert the Filter as step 2, right after the trigger, and the Zone lookup table next to the fee lookup.
In the 0.4 workbook, add a Logistics tab with headers in row 1: name, phone, delivery date, area, zone, product, quantity, total.

Write the truth table first (≤ 50,000 inside → C; ≤ 50,000 outside → B; > 50,000 inside → A; > 50,000 outside → A with its own Logistics row; missing area → C via the fee/zone fallbacks). Decide now that Priority handles its own logistics.
Connect Google Forms, Google Sheets and Gmail with the Harvest Lane business Google account. Rename every Formatter, Filter and Path step as listed so the Zap reads like a recipe.
Test each step, then publish. Share it from the Zap's menu → Share to get the template link.
items.test: Submit one form per truth-table row: a ₦26,500 Bodija order (C · Standard), a ₦13,500 Oyo town order (B · Outside zone: Orders + Logistics rows, no email), a ₦92,000 Bodija order (A · Priority, PRIORITY email, no Logistics row), a ₦92,000 Oyo order (A only, PRIORITY email plus a Logistics row, never two Orders rows), and one with "Test" in the name (Filtered, no rows, no task). In Zap history each real order shows exactly one branch taken.
items.tasks: About three tasks per order (the Products lookup plus two app steps in the branch taken), four for a big out-of-zone order, and none for a filtered test order; Filter, Formatter and Paths use no tasks.

walk.title: Build it: route every order to the right place
walk.sample: Five orders: ₦26,500 Bodija · ₦13,500 Oyo town · ₦92,000 Bodija · ₦92,000 Oyo · "Test" order

steps.say: We start from the 1.2 order Zap. Same trigger, the order form with its Area dropdown. Every order still enters on one track; we're adding a junction.
Right after the trigger, a filter drops test orders. They stop here, before any task is used, and show as Filtered in Zap history.
The cleaning and pricing steps from 1.2 stay as they were: clean phone, clean date, then the price from the Products sheet.
Next to the fee lookup, add a second lookup table that turns the area into one clean word, inside or outside. The fallback means a new area is always outside.
show: Bodija, Mokola, Ring Road, Challenge → inside

steps.say: The total is still a plain number. That matters, because the path rules compare numbers, and a naira-formatted total is text.
Before building the paths, write the truth table. A big order from outside the zone goes to Priority, which logs its own logistics, so nothing alerts twice.
Branch A, Priority: the total, the plain number from step eight, greater than fifty thousand.
Inside Priority we save the order row, then email Tolu with PRIORITY in the subject so it's read now, not in three hours.
show: Subject: PRIORITY · New order · name · date · total

steps.say: A small filter inside the branch adds a Logistics row only when the big order is outside the zone.
Branch B, Outside zone, needs both conditions. Less than fifty thousand and one means fifty thousand or less, so a big outside order can't match A and B together.
Branch B saves the order, then adds a Logistics row, so the rider plan for Oyo town is known the night before.
Branch C is the fallback. It runs only when no other branch matched, so surprising data never disappears silently.
show: Path C · Standard: set as fallback

steps.say: Now test every row of the truth table. In Zap history, each real order must show exactly one branch, and the test order shows Filtered. Then publish.

walk.end: Five orders, five right answers, and not one double alert. Write your truth table, then build it yourself.

items.name: HL · Website order → checked + saved
items.what: The website posts each order as JSON to a Zapier webhook. A Code step parses the raw body, checks the shared token, recalculates every line and the total, and returns valid/errors. Valid orders become one Orders row plus one Order_Items row per item; anything else emails Tolu the exact problems.
steps: 1 · Trigger · Webhooks by Zapier › Catch Raw Hook: copy the hook URL Zapier shows and treat it as a secret (share only with the website's developer). Test trigger after sending the good sample from Hoppscotch (POST, Content-Type: application/json).
3 · Paths by Zapier ("Valid or not"):
3A · Path A · Valid: Only continue if… [2. Valid] (Boolean) Is true.

steps: 1 · Trigger · Gmail › New Labeled Email: Label = Customers (a Gmail filter applies it, as in 1.1). Test with an email from your 0.5 Silver list.

2 · Action · AI by Zapier › Analyze and Return Data (rename "Triage email"): Model = Standard; Prompt (insert the subject and plain body with /):
You triage customer emails for Harvest Lane, a fresh-produce
delivery business in Ibadan, Nigeria. Customers write in English,
Nigerian Pidgin or Yoruba.
Read the email below and fill in the output fields.
- category: order (new or change), complaint, question, or other.

- summary: at most 20 words, plain English, no greeting.

3 · Action · Zapier Tables › Create Record: Table = HL Inbox; received_at = [1. Date]; from_email = [1. From Email]; category = [2. category]; summary = [2. summary]; urgency = [2. urgency]; phone = [2. phone]; status = New; handled_by left empty.

items.name: HL Customer Helper (Zapier Agent)
items.what: A Zapier Agent that wakes on new question records in HL Inbox, reads prices only from the Products table and fees and areas only from the Delivery Areas table, writes a short draft reply (or HANDOVER for refunds, complaints and anything else) back to the record with status Draft ready, and can never send, delete or touch payments.
steps: 1 · Create agent: Zapier Agents › New agent; name = HL Customer Helper.

2 · Instructions: paste exactly:
# INSTRUCTIONS
You answer customer questions for Harvest Lane, a produce delivery
business in Ibadan. Answer only about prices, delivery areas, fees and
delivery days.
- Get prices ONLY from the Products table. Never guess a price.
- Get delivery fees and areas ONLY from the Delivery Areas table.
- If a question is about a refund, complaint or anything else,
  write "HANDOVER" and a one-line summary for staff.
- Write a short, friendly draft reply. Do not send anything.
- Save the draft to HL Inbox with status "Draft ready" (add this option to the status dropdown from 1.5).

3 · Trigger: Zapier Tables › New Record in HL Inbox, only where category = question (if the trigger has no condition option, add to the instructions: "If the record's category is not question, stop and do nothing.").
4 · Tool (allowed): Zapier Tables › Find Record in Products (search by name; returns sku and price_ngn).
5 · Tool (allowed): Zapier Tables › Find Record in Delivery Areas (search by area; returns fee_ngn and delivery_days).
6 · Tool (allowed): Zapier Tables › Update Record in HL Inbox, limited to the fields draft_reply and status (set status to Draft ready).
7 · NOT given (do not add): Gmail send, Sheets delete, anything payment-related (Paystack, refunds), web search or browse.
8 · Approval: Kemi reads each draft on the HL Staff Desk and sends it with the Approve & send button from 1.5 Gold; the agent never sends.

Show draft_reply on the Staff Desk page next to the Approve & send button.

items.name: HL · Readable receipt
items.what: The 2.2 solved problem: for each new Orders row, one Google Sheets · Update a Row fills phone_clean (+234 format), first_name, delivery_day (next day, never a Sunday) and a readable receipt_text, all with functions inside the fields. 2 credits per order however many functions it uses. It reproduces the lesson's "Hi Mrs!" title bug on purpose; fixing it is the Silver mission.
build: 1 · Google Sheets › Watch New Rows: business Google connection; Spreadsheet = Harvest Lane; Sheet = Orders; Table contains headers = Yes; Limit = 10; start From now on.
2 · Google Sheets › Update a Row: same spreadsheet; Sheet = Orders; Row number = 1. Row number (the trigger's row number); leave A–N empty so the original columns are untouched, and fill only:

phone_clean (column O) = {{if(substring(replace(1.phone; /[^0-9]/g; emptystring); 0; 1) = "0"; "+234" + substring(replace(1.phone; /[^0-9]/g; emptystring); 1; 20); "+" + replace(1.phone; /[^0-9]/g; emptystring))}}
first_name (column P) = {{startcase(lower(get(split(trim(1.customer_name); " "); 1)))}}
delivery_day (column Q) = {{if(formatDate(addDays(1.created_at; 1); "d") = "0"; formatDate(addDays(1.created_at; 2); "dddd D MMM"); formatDate(addDays(1.created_at; 1); "dddd D MMM"))}}

receipt_text (column R) = Hi {{startcase(lower(get(split(trim(1.customer_name); " "); 1)))}}! Order {{1.order_id}} received. [new line] Total: ₦{{formatNumber(1.total; 0; "."; ",")}} [new line] Delivery: {{if(formatDate(addDays(1.created_at; 1); "d") = "0"; formatDate(addDays(1.created_at; 2); "dddd D MMM"); formatDate(addDays(1.created_at; 1); "dddd D MMM"))}}, {{ifempty(1.delivery_window; "time to be confirmed")}}. [new line] Thank you for choosing Harvest Lane.
Arguments are separated by semicolons; emptystring is Make's keyword for ""; substring counts from 0, get() from 1; MM is month, mm is minutes, d is the weekday number (0 = Sunday).
Optional title fix (Silver mission): inside first_name, wrap trim(1.customer_name) as replace(trim(1.customer_name); /^(mr|mrs|miss|dr|chief)\.?\s+/i; emptystring) before split().
setup: In Make, set your organisation and profile time zone to Africa/Lagos before running anything with dates (2.2).

steps.say: Same trigger as 2.1: Watch New Rows on the Orders tab, starting from now on.
We add just one more module, Update a Row, and point it at the trigger's own row number, so we write back to the same order.
We leave the original columns empty so nothing gets overwritten. Only the four new columns, O to R, get filled.
For the phone, strip everything that isn't a digit, then swap a leading zero for plus two three four. One format, so one customer never becomes three.
For the first name: trim, split on the space, take item one, then tidy the case. Remember, get counts from one in Make.
Delivery is the next day, unless that's a Sunday, when it moves to Monday. The little d token gives the weekday number, and zero means Sunday.
The receipt mixes plain text with formulas. The naira sign and commas are for people only; the total column keeps a plain number you can sum.
Watch the separators: Make uses semicolons between arguments, and emptystring for an empty value. Commas make the formula invalid.

steps.say: We start with a search, not a watch. Search Rows finds every order whose delivery date is tomorrow, one bundle per order.
show: Google Sheets › Search Rows · Sheet: Orders

steps.say: It runs once a day at eight in the evening. One search a night is far cheaper than polling every fifteen minutes.
On the link before the router we drop cancelled orders. Filters cost nothing, and junk stops here before any work is done.
show: status · Not equal to (case insensitive) · Cancelled

steps.say: Now the router. Write each route's rule in words first. These routes are additive: one order can take two routes when it needs two jobs.
show: 1 Rider list · 2 Reminder · 3 Big order · Fallback

steps.say: Route one, the rider list: every order that will be delivered. Paid, or a standing customer, so it's an OR group.
Those orders become a row on the Deliveries tab, with what the rider needs: name, phone and delivery window.
show: Google Sheets › Add a Row · Sheet: Deliveries

steps.say: Route two, reminders: new orders that aren't standing customers. Both conditions must be true, so they sit in one AND group.
The customer gets a polite email with their total and the payment link, so they can pay before the riders go out.
show: Subject: Harvest Lane · please pay for order {{1.order_id}}

steps.say: Route three alerts Tolu about any order over fifty thousand naira. Use the numeric operator here. A text comparison would let a nine thousand naira order through.
The alert goes to Tolu on Telegram. The bot token lives only in Make's connection screen, never in a message or a sheet.
show: Telegram Bot › Send a Text Message

steps.say: The last route is the fallback. Mark it as fallback, and anything that matched no rule lands in Needs checking instead of vanishing.
show: Add a Row · Sheet: Needs checking

steps.say: Remember, routes never merge back. Anything every order needs, like a log, belongs before the router.
Run once with the six test rows and read the counts: two, two, two and one. That's one credit for the search and seven for the work. The filter and router are free.
steps.data: nothing twice on the rider list

steps.say: Everything here runs in Paystack test mode with test keys. No real money moves. First, create a data store called processed_payments, keyed by the payment reference.
The trigger is a custom webhook. Paste its address into Paystack's test webhook setting, and post the sample once so Make learns the fields.
Reply straight away with a two hundred and ok. A fast reply stops Paystack retrying and piling up duplicates.
On the next link, a filter lets only successful charges through. Any other event, like a transfer, stops here.
Now the memory. Check whether we've already handled this reference.
show: Data store › Check the existence of a record

steps.say: Continue only if it's new. A duplicate webhook stops here, before any work or a second receipt.
Never trust the webhook body. We phone Paystack's verify endpoint with the reference. The secret key lives in a keychain, never typed into a header field.
show: HTTP › Make an API Key Auth request · GET

steps.say: Only Paystack's own answer decides. A fake payment someone posted has no successful transaction, so it stops at this filter.
Find the order in the sheet using the order ID we put in the payment's metadata.
A router checks the amount. Paystack counts in kobo, so the order total times a hundred must match exactly.
On the matching route, mark the order Paid with the time.
Then remember the payment in the data store, so if the same webhook ever arrives again, it's harmless.
And send exactly one receipt, reusing the readable receipt text from 2.2.
If the amount is wrong, the other route emails Tolu instead, and the order is not marked Paid.

A booked order goes on the Deliveries tab with the courier reference and the rain chance.
A sheet write rarely fails, usually a quota blip, so it gets Break with two retries.

items.name: HL · Supplier invoices → books, checked
items.what: Each new file in Supplier invoices is read by an AI model into fixed JSON, parsed, and checked by arithmetic: line maths, lines = subtotal, subtotal + VAT = total, an invoice number and nothing unreadable. Clean invoices go to Supplier_Invoices and Invoice_Lines; anything doubtful goes to Needs_Review with exact reasons and an email to Tolu.
setup: Connections: Google Drive, Google Sheets and Gmail with the Harvest Lane business Google account; OpenAI (your own API key, stored in the connection) in "Read invoice (AI)". Replace YOUR_MODEL with a vision-capable model.
In "Watch Supplier invoices" pick the Drive folder your 1.1 Zap fills (replace YOUR_SUPPLIER_INVOICES_FOLDER_ID). Choose "From now on" when asked where to start.

In "Read invoice (AI)" add the downloaded file to the user message (image/file input = Download a File → Data). If your OpenAI module can't take PDFs, insert Make's AI Content Extractor (extract text from a document) after Download a File and map its text into the user message instead.
In "Parse JSON" click Add data structure → Generate, and paste the clean Farmgate sample from the lesson's playground (add "unreadable_parts": []).

Spreadsheet (replace YOUR_BOOKS_SHEET_ID) with tabs: Supplier_Invoices = A supplier, B invoice_number, C invoice_date, D subtotal, E vat, F total, G drive_link, H added_at, I note. Invoice_Lines = A invoice_number, B supplier, C invoice_date, D description, E qty, F unit_price, G line_total. Needs_Review = A file, B supplier, C invoice_number, D total, E reasons, F drive_link, G added_at, H status.
Scenario settings: Allow storing of incomplete executions (for the Break on the AI step). Schedule: every 60 minutes, 08:00–18:00, Monday–Saturday.
Privacy (0.6): test with invoices you typed or printed yourself; never real supplier bank details.
items.test: Drop five sample invoices in the folder (two software PDFs, a scanned PDF, a photo of a printed invoice, and a handwritten slip with no number) and Run once: four rows in Supplier_Invoices with their lines in Invoice_Lines, and the slip in Needs_Review with "No invoice number" plus the unclear digit, and one email to Tolu. Change one line_total in a typed invoice (56,000 for 65,000): it lands in Needs_Review with "Line maths: …".

2 · Google Drive › Download a File "Download a File": File ID {{1.id}}.

3 · OpenAI › Create a Completion (chat) "Read invoice (AI)": model YOUR_MODEL; temperature 0; response format JSON object; max tokens 2000; system message = the lesson prompt ("You extract supplier invoices for Harvest Lane … Never guess a number."); user message "Invoice file: {{1.name}} (attached)." with the file from module 2 attached.

Error handler on 3 · Gmail › Send an email "Alert Tolu (AI step)": Subject Invoice reader failed · {{1.name}}; Body {{error.type}}: {{error.message}} + the Drive link → Break: automatic completion Yes, 2 attempts, every 15 minutes.
4 · JSON › Parse JSON "Parse JSON": JSON string {{3.result}}; data structure generated from the clean Farmgate sample.
40 · Router "Any lines?" (a guard so an invoice with no lines can't vanish in an empty iterator).
Route 1 · filter on 40→5 "Has lines": {{length(4.lines)}} Numeric: Greater than 0.
5 · Flow control › Iterator "Iterator · lines": Array {{4.lines}}.

6 · Tools › Set variable "Line check": name line_problem; lifetime one cycle; value {{if(abs(5.qty * 5.unit_price - 5.line_total) > 1; 5.description + ": " + 5.qty + " x " + 5.unit_price + " is not " + 5.line_total; emptystring)}}.

7 · Flow control › Array aggregator "Array aggregator · lines": Source module 5 (Iterator); fields line_total (5) and line_problem (6). This one aggregator does the lesson's Numeric aggregator (SUM) and text collection in a single pass.
8 · Tools › Set multiple variables "Sum and bad lines": lines_sum = {{sum(map(7.array; "line_total"))}}; bad_lines = {{join(remove(map(7.array; "line_problem"); emptystring); "; ")}}.

9 · Tools › Set multiple variables "Verdict": review_reasons = one text built from five checks: bad_lines not empty → "Line maths: …"; abs(lines_sum − subtotal) > 1 → "Lines add up to … but subtotal is …"; abs(subtotal + vat − total) > 1 → "Subtotal + VAT does not equal total."; invoice_number empty → "No invoice number."; unreadable_parts not empty → "Unreadable: …". Empty review_reasons means every check passed.
10 · Router "Save or review".

Route Auto-save · filter on 10→11 "Auto-save" (no bad lines AND sum = subtotal ±1 AND subtotal + vat = total ±1 AND invoice_number exists AND unreadable_parts empty): {{length(trim(9.review_reasons))}} Numeric: Equal to 0 → 11 · Google Sheets › Add a Row "Add to Supplier_Invoices": supplier, invoice_number, invoice_date, subtotal, vat, total, drive_link {{1.webViewLink}}, added_at now, note {{if(ifempty(4.vat; 0) > 0 & abs(4.vat - 4.subtotal * 0.075) > 1; "VAT isn't 7.5%"; emptystring)}} → 12 · Iterator "Iterator · lines to save" {{4.lines}} → 13 · Google Sheets › Add a Row "Add to Invoice_Lines": invoice_number, supplier, invoice_date, description, qty, unit_price, line_total.

Route 2 of 40 · filter "No lines": {{length(4.lines)}} Equal to 0 → 16 · Add a Row "Needs_Review (no lines)" (reason "No line items could be read." + unreadable_parts) → 17 · Gmail "Email Tolu (no lines)".

walk.title: Build it: invoices into the books, checked
walk.sample: Farmgate Supplies FG-0192 · 3 lines · subtotal 290,000 · VAT 21,750 · total 311,750

steps.say: We watch the Supplier invoices folder your 1.1 Zap already fills, starting from now on, and run hourly in business hours.
show: Google Drive › Watch Files in a Folder

steps.say: Download the file itself, so the AI can read the actual invoice, not just its name.
Sage reads it. We use our own provider connection, a vision-capable model, temperature zero, and JSON mode so the answer is valid JSON.
show: OpenAI › Create a Completion · model: YOUR_MODEL
User message: the downloaded file attached

steps.say: The prompt fixes the shape, with line items so there's something to check. And one rule matters most: if a value is unclear, use null and say why. Never guess a number.
show: Return ONLY JSON: supplier, invoice_number, lines[], …

steps.say: If the AI provider is down, an error route emails Tolu what failed.
Then Break with two retries, so invoices wait instead of disappearing. Remember to allow incomplete executions in the settings.
Parse JSON with a data structure generated from the clean sample. Now supplier, totals and the lines list are fields you can map.
show: Data structure: generated from clean Farmgate sample

steps.say: A small guard router first: if no lines could be read at all, the invoice goes straight to review instead of vanishing in an empty iterator.
Now Weave checks the arithmetic. The iterator splits the lines, one bundle each.
For each line, quantity times unit price must equal the line total, within one naira. If not, we note the problem in words.
show: line_problem: abs(qty × unit_price − line_total) > 1 → describe it

steps.say: An array aggregator, sourced from the iterator, squeezes the lines back together, carrying each line total and any problem.
Then we add up the lines and collect the bad ones.

The verdict collects every reason to doubt the invoice: bad lines, lines not matching the subtotal, subtotal plus VAT not matching the total, no invoice number, or anything unreadable. Empty means it all adds up.
Only a clean invoice skips a human. It's saved to Supplier_Invoices, with a note if VAT isn't seven and a half percent, and each line goes to Invoice_Lines.
show: Add a Row · Supplier_Invoices, then Invoice_Lines per line

steps.say: Anything doubtful goes to Needs_Review with the exact reasons and the Drive link, and Tolu gets one email. One misread digit is caught here, not in the books.

walk.end: Drop in your five sample invoices, including one with a wrong line total, and check each lands on the route you expected, with clear reasons.

{ "supplier": string, "invoice_number": string|null,

  "lines": [ { "description": string, "qty": number,

items.name: HL · Ask Weave agent + its read-only tool
items.what: The bonus "Ask Weave" agent: a Make AI Agent that answers Tolu's spending questions using one read-only tool, this scenario, which searches Invoice_Lines by supplier, product and date range and returns the total, line count and invoice numbers. The agent and its Telegram runner are set up by hand from the steps below.
setup: Import this blueprint as a new scenario named "HL · Tool · Supplier spend lookup (read-only)". Connect Google Sheets (business account) and pick the books spreadsheet (YOUR_BOOKS_SHEET_ID) and the Invoice_Lines tab from the invoice scenario.

Scenario inputs (scenario settings → Scenario inputs and outputs): inputs supplier (text, optional, "Supplier name or part of it, e.g. Farmgate"), product (text, optional, "Product word, e.g. tomatoes"), date_from (text, required, "YYYY-MM-DD"), date_to (text, required, "YYYY-MM-DD"). Outputs total_ngn (number), line_count (number), invoices (text), suppliers (text). Scheduling: On demand. Turn the scenario on.

Scenario description (the agent reads it to choose the tool): "Read-only. Returns how much Harvest Lane spent with suppliers, from the Invoice_Lines sheet, filtered by supplier, product and date range. Returns nothing when no lines match."

Create the agent: Make → AI Agents → Create agent. Name Ask Weave; model connection = your AI provider (your own key) and a capable model; system prompt exactly: "You answer Tolu's questions about supplier spending using only the tools provided. Never change data. If the tools can't answer, say so." Add one tool: Scenarios → HL · Tool · Supplier spend lookup (read-only). Add no module or MCP tools that can write, update, delete or send.

Create the runner scenario "HL · Ask Weave (Telegram)": Telegram Bot › Watch Updates (your bot) → filter: Message › Chat ID equal to Tolu's chat ID (YOUR_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID) → Make AI Agents › Run an agent: agent Ask Weave; message {{1.message.text}}; thread ID {{1.message.chat.id}} → Telegram Bot › Send a Text Message or a Reply: chat ID {{1.message.chat.id}}, text = the agent's response.
Before quoting a client, check Make's current credit use for agents and the model's token price (Card 1).
items.test: From Tolu's Telegram ask "How much did we spend on tomatoes from Farmgate in October?": the reply gives the naira total and invoice numbers, matching a manual SUMIFS on Invoice_Lines, and the tool scenario's history shows one run with those inputs. Ask "Delete the duplicate Farmgate row": the agent says it can't change data. Message the bot from another account: nothing runs past the chat ID filter.

items.name: HL · Morning weather → Sheet
items.what: Every morning at 06:30 Lagos time, fetches Ibadan's forecast from Open-Meteo, shapes it into one row with rider advice, and appends it to the HL Weather sheet.
setup: Start n8n in Docker with a volume and your timezone: run docker volume create n8n_data, then docker run -it --name n8n -p 5678:5678 -e GENERIC_TIMEZONE="Africa/Lagos" -e TZ="Africa/Lagos" -e N8N_ENFORCE_SETTINGS_FILE_PERMISSIONS=true -e N8N_RUNNERS_ENABLED=true -v n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n n8nio/n8n (or open an n8n Cloud trial instead).
Open http://localhost:5678 and create the owner account with a strong password.
Create a Google Sheet called HL Weather whose first tab (Sheet1) has the headers date, max_temp_c, rain_chance, rain_mm, advice in row 1.

Create a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential called "Google Sheets" (Cloud: sign in with Google; self-hosted: create an OAuth client in Google Cloud Console and paste n8n's OAuth Redirect URL exactly). Select it in the Google Sheets node.
Replace YOUR_SHEET_ID in the Google Sheets node with your HL Weather sheet's ID (the long string in its URL). If your tab isn't called Sheet1, pick it from the list.
Save, then Publish the workflow so the 06:30 schedule runs on its own.
items.test: Click Execute workflow: the HTTP Request output shows daily lists such as temperature_2m_max: [30.4], Edit Fields shows one item with five fields (numbers without brackets), and one row lands in HL Weather. After publishing, Executions should show a run you didn't start at 06:30 the next morning.

walk.title: Build it: the morning weather log
walk.sample: Ibadan forecast for 2026-10-05 · max 30.4 °C · rain chance 78% · 5.3 mm

steps.say: Start n8n in Docker with a volume and the Lagos timezone. The volume keeps your workflows and credentials when the container restarts, and the timezone makes six thirty mean six thirty in Ibadan.
Our trigger is a schedule: every day at six thirty in the morning, before the riders head out.
Next, an HTTP Request to Open-Meteo for Ibadan's forecast. It needs no key, so there's no credential here.
Click Execute step and read the JSON. Notice each daily value is a list, even with one day of forecast.
Edit Fields shapes one tidy item. We use square bracket zero to take the number out of each list, and every value is set to Expression, not Fixed.
The advice field turns the numbers into something a rider can act on. Sixty percent or more means pack tarpaulins and start early.
show: ? "Rain likely: pack tarpaulins, start deliveries early"

steps.say: Set the number fields' type to Number, so the sheet can chart and sum them later.
Finally, append the row to the HL Weather sheet. The Google login lives in a credential, never typed into a field.
Mapping is set to Map Automatically. Because our field names match the headers exactly, every column fills itself.
show: Headers: date · max_temp_c · rain_chance · rain_mm · advice

steps.say: Execute the workflow once, then Save and Publish. Saving alone never runs on a schedule. One run a day is about thirty executions a month, however many nodes it has.

walk.end: Execute the workflow, check the new row, then publish it and look in Executions tomorrow for a run you didn't start.

items.name: HL · Tomorrow's order messages → Outbox
items.what: Gets tomorrow's orders, looks up each customer, builds a WhatsApp-ready message and a wa.me click-to-chat link per order, and appends them to an Outbox sheet without sending anything.
setup: Create one Google Sheet with three tabs: Orders (order_id, customer_id, items, total, delivery_date as YYYY-MM-DD), Customers (customer_id, name, phone, area) and Outbox (order_id, phone, message, wa_link). Use test data only, with phones like +2348000000001.
Create a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential called "Google Sheets" and select it in Orders, Find customer and Outbox.
Replace YOUR_SHEET_ID in all three Google Sheets nodes with your sheet's ID.
The Orders and Find customer nodes have pinned sample data. Keep it to build and test; unpin both (pin icon in the Output panel) when you want to read your real sheet.
When it works, replace the Manual Trigger with a Schedule Trigger at 18:00 and publish.
items.test: Click Execute workflow with the pinned data: Outbox gets three rows, each with a different customer (Mrs Adebayo, Mr Okafor, Iya Basira), their own order number, a formatted total such as ₦34,000, and a wa.me link. To see the missing-customer case, unpin Find customer, add an Orders row for tomorrow whose customer_id isn't in Customers, and run again: that order still reaches the Outbox with Hello Customer instead of disappearing.

walk.title: Build it: a WhatsApp-ready message for every order
walk.sample: Three orders for tomorrow · HL-0071 Mrs Adebayo ₦34,000 · HL-0072 Mr Okafor ₦4,000 · HL-0073 Iya Basira ₦21,000

steps.say: We build with a Manual Trigger, so nothing runs on its own while we work. Once it's right, we swap in a schedule at six in the evening.
Get the rows from the Orders tab where the delivery date is tomorrow. Rename the node Orders first, because expressions refer to nodes by name.
show: Google Sheets › Get Row(s) · Sheet: Orders

steps.say: Execute it once, then pin the output. From now on we build without calling Google, and we can edit the pinned data to invent test cases.
Look up each order's customer on the Customers tab. It runs once per order, and each result stays linked to its own order.
steps.data: 3 items · Mrs Adebayo, Mr Okafor, Iya Basira

steps.say: Turn on Always Output Data in its settings. Otherwise an order with an unknown customer silently disappears.
In Build message, dollar json is the customer, because that's the node just before. To reach the order, we follow the item link back with Orders dot item.
The message mixes text and expressions: the name with a fallback, the items, a total with proper commas, and a friendly delivery day.
Use dot item, not dot first. First would give every message item zero's data. Step through items zero, one and two in the preview to be sure each is different.
Fields in one Edit Fields node can't see each other, so a second node builds the one-tap link from the finished message. WhatsApp wants the number without the plus, and the text URL-encoded.
Append each message to the Outbox tab. Nothing is sent yet; Tolu reviews and taps the link.
show: Google Sheets › Append Row · Sheet: Outbox

steps.say: Now test the edge case: add a pinned order whose customer doesn't exist. Thanks to Always Output Data, it still reaches the Outbox as Hello Customer, so Tolu can fix the record.

walk.end: Execute the workflow with the pinned orders and check that each Outbox row has its own customer, order number and total.

parameters.content:
## HL · Tomorrow's order messages → Outbox (Lesson 3.2)
For every order delivering tomorrow: look up the customer, build a WhatsApp-ready message and a one-tap wa.me link, and append them to the Outbox sheet. Nothing is sent.

**Credential:** Google Sheets (OAuth2), selected in all three Sheets nodes.
**Placeholder:** YOUR_SHEET_ID (one workbook with tabs Orders, Customers, Outbox).

Orders and Find customer come with **pinned test data** (3 orders, 3 customers), so manual runs never call Google. Unpin both (pin icon in Output) to use your real sheet. Published runs always use real data.

Once it works, swap the Manual Trigger for a Schedule Trigger at 18:00.

assignments.name: message

parameters.content:
## Why .item, not .first()
Build message's input is Find customer, so $json is the customer. The order is reached with $('Orders').item, which follows the item link back to *this* customer's order. .first() would give every message item 0's data.

Find customer has **Always Output Data** on (Settings), so an order whose customer_id has no match still produces a message ("Hello Customer") instead of vanishing.

Step through items 0, 1 and 2 in the Input panel: each preview must show a different customer.

items.name: HL · Monday payment reminders
items.what: Every Monday at 09:00, removes paid customers from the unpaid invoices with Merge, sets aside rows with no phone, writes reminders to a Sent log in batches of 20 with a 60-second wait, and emails Tolu one summary.
setup: Create one Google Sheet with tabs Invoices (invoice_id, customer_id, name, phone, amount, pay_link, status), Payments (reference, customer_id, amount, paid_at), Fix list (same columns as Invoices) and Sent log (customer_id, phone, message, sent_at). Test data only.
Create a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential called "Google Sheets" and select it in Invoices, Payments, Fix list and Send (log).
Create a Gmail OAuth2 credential called "Gmail" and select it in Summary email.
Replace YOUR_SHEET_ID in all four Google Sheets nodes with your sheet's ID.
Replace YOUR_EMAIL in Summary email with the address that should receive the summary (your own while testing).
Invoices and Payments have pinned sample data for building; unpin them to read your real sheets.
For testing, set Loop Over Items batch size to 2 and Wait 60 s to 5 seconds; set them back to 20 and 60 before you save and publish.
items.test: With the pinned data and batch size 2, wait 5 s, click Execute workflow: Chef Tunde (who paid) is skipped, Mr Okafor (no phone) lands on the Fix list, the other three get rows in the Sent log with sent_at times in clusters of two about 5 seconds apart, and exactly one summary email arrives saying Reminders sent: 3.

walk.title: Build it: polite reminders, paced, payers skipped
walk.sample: Five unpaid invoices · Chef Tunde has paid since · Mr Okafor has no phone · batch size 2, wait 5 seconds for testing

steps.say: Every Monday at nine, one trigger starts two sources side by side.
The first source is every unpaid invoice. Pin its output while you build.
show: Google Sheets › Get Row(s) · Sheet: Invoices

steps.say: The second is the payments log, so we can see who has paid since the invoice went out.
show: Google Sheets › Get Row(s) · Sheet: Payments

steps.say: Merge crosses off the payers. Match on customer ID, never on names, because there can be two Mrs Adebayos.
Keep only the non-matches, with data from Input one: invoices with no payment. Payers are removed before a single message is built.
An IF checks there's a phone number to reach.
Anyone without a number goes on the Fix list for Tolu, so nobody is silently dropped.
Now pace the sending. Loop Over Items hands out batches of twenty, from the provider's limit, not a guess. For testing, use two.
From the loop output, build a gentle reminder with the name, invoice number, amount and the pay link.
For practice, Send only writes to a Sent log with a timestamp. No message reaches a customer until we swap in a real messaging node.
Wait sixty seconds, inside the loop. Then drag Wait's output back into Loop Over Items, or only the first batch ever goes.
show: Wait → back into Loop Over Items

steps.say: The done output fires once after the last batch, carrying every item. Turn on Execute Once, so Tolu gets one summary, not one per customer.
When the test looks right, put the batch back to twenty and the wait to sixty seconds, then save and publish.

walk.end: Run it with the pinned data, then check the Sent log times come in clusters of two and exactly one summary arrives.

parameters.content:
## HL · Monday payment reminders (Lesson 3.3)
Monday 09:00: unpaid invoices minus anyone who has paid (Merge, keep non-matches from Input 1), set aside anyone with no phone (Fix list), then remind in batches of 20 with a 60 s wait, and email Tolu one summary.

"Send (log)" only writes to a Sent log sheet: no message reaches a customer. A real messaging node comes in 3.4 / Boss 3.

**Credentials:** Google Sheets (OAuth2) in all four Sheets nodes; Gmail (OAuth2) in Summary email.
**Placeholders:** YOUR_SHEET_ID (tabs Invoices, Payments, Fix list, Sent log), YOUR_EMAIL (Tolu's address) in Summary email.

**Test first:** batch size 2 and wait 5 s. Put them back to 20 and 60 before publishing.
